# Captured lab output

- `arista_aspath.json`: cEOS 4.36.3M, 27 October 2026, `show ip bgp regexp _13335$ | json`. Retains one complete route entry from 2,544 entries. No route fields are synthesized.
- `arista_traceroute.txt`: cEOS 4.36.3M, 27 October 2026, `traceroute ip 1.1.1.1 source 10.250.7.1`. Complete output, including MPLS annotations and multiple responders.
- `bird_traceroute.txt`, `openbgpd_traceroute.txt`, `vyos_traceroute.txt`: complete built-in traceroute responses from the corresponding lab devices, 27 October 2026, target `1.1.1.1`. Each capture includes all nine hops and the destination.

Synthetic cases in tests are explicitly separate from these device captures. Issues #22, #23 and #25 track the remaining hardware and configuration matrix.

## 28 October 2026 captures

Text fixtures retain all output lines and column spacing. Trailing end-of-line whitespace is removed from the Huawei text captures.

- `huawei-vrp/`: complete CE12800 V200R005C10SPC607B607 responses. `route4.txt` and `route6.txt` use `display bgp [ipv6] routing-table <target> | no-more` for `1.1.1.1` and `2606:4700::1111`. `aspath4.txt` and `aspath6.txt` use `display bgp [ipv6] routing-table regular-expression _13335$`. `community4.txt` and `community6.txt` use `display bgp [ipv6] routing-table community 37195:302`. `trace.txt` uses `tracert -w 500 -q 1 -f 1 -a 10.250.8.1 1.1.1.1`. The lab advertises a bounded route subset to this emulated control plane. Captures contain two IPv4 AS-path routes, one IPv6 AS-path route, 40 IPv4 community routes, and zero IPv6 community routes.
- Huawei community brief output contains communities but omits AS paths. Huawei AS-path brief output contains AS paths but omits communities. Tests preserve these omissions. BGP `valid` is not an RPKI validation result.
- `frr-live/`: complete lab FRR responses from `vtysh -c 'show bgp ipv4 unicast 1.1.1.0/24 json'`, `vtysh -c 'show bgp ipv6 unicast 2606:4700::/44 json'`, and `traceroute -n -w 1 -q 1 -s 10.250.1.1 1.1.1.1`.
- `arista_live_route.json`: complete cEOS 4.36.3M response from `show ip bgp 1.1.1.1 | json`. The live-provider replay uses this capture with the matching FRR and Huawei captures.
- `mikrotik-live/`: complete RouterOS 7.16.2 raw responses extracted from the lab JSONL query log. Each fixture retains its original timestamp, device, and query. The traceroute fixture includes all intermediate screen updates; the test runs the normal cleanup plugin before parsing.
- `frr_route_empty.json`, `frr_route_local.json`, `frr_route_inaccessible_nexthop.json`: complete FRRouting 10.2.2 responses from `vtysh -c 'show bgp ipv4 unicast <target> json'`. Targets are `100.64.0.0/10` (not in the table), `192.0.2.1` (locally sourced by a temporary `network 192.0.2.0/24` with a blackhole route) and `198.18.10.1` (injected from the core with unreachable next hop `10.99.99.99`). Both lab changes were reverted after capture. Issue #39.
- `arista_large_community.json`: complete cEOS 4.36.3M response from `show ip bgp 198.51.100.0/24 detail | json`. The core injected the route with `community 65000:100` and `large-community 65000:1:1`, then withdrew it after capture. Issue #38.
- `vyos-live/`: VyOS 1.5 stream responses from the lab router over SSH, using the FRR shell. `route4.json` and `route6.json` are complete responses from `vtysh -c 'show bgp ipv4 unicast 1.1.1.1 json'` and `vtysh -c 'show bgp ipv6 unicast 2606:4700::1111 json'`. `aspath4.json` (`regexp _37239_13335$`) and `community4.json` (`community 13335:10045`) keep the first five prefixes of 2,214 and 1,198 returned prefixes; route entries are unchanged. Issue #54.
- `openbgpd-live/`: OpenBGPD 8.8 responses from `bgpctl -j show rib detail <family> <filter>` on the lab router. `route4.json` (`inet 1.1.1.1`), `route6.json` (`inet6 2606:4700::1111`), `empty.json` (`inet 100.64.0.0/10`) and `large_community.json` (`inet 198.51.100.1`, injected from the core with `community 65000:100` and `large-community 65000:1:1`, then withdrawn) are complete. `aspath4.json` (`source-as 13335`) and `community4.json` (`community 37195:302`) keep the first five of 31,159 and 27,350 RIB entries; entries are unchanged. Issue #55.
- `bird-live/`: BIRD 2.17.2 responses from `birdc` on the lab router. `route4.txt` (`show route for 1.1.1.1 all`), `route6.txt` (`show route for 2606:4700::1111 all`), `empty.txt` (`show route all where bgp_path ~ [= * 4200000000 =]`) and `large_community.txt` (`show route for 198.51.100.1 all`, injected from the core with a community, a large community and MED 5, then withdrawn) are complete. `aspath4.txt` (`bgp_path ~ [= * 13335 =]`) and `community4.txt` (`(37195,302) ~ bgp_community`) keep every path of the first five of 5,463 and 27,358 prefixes; lines are unchanged. Issue #56.
- `arista_vrf_local_route.json`: complete cEOS 4.36.3M response from `show ip bgp 198.51.100.1 vrf LAB | json`. VRF `LAB` originates `198.51.100.0/24` from a Null0 static route, so the path is locally originated and has no `localPreference`. Issue #50.

## Lab test routes (issues #22 and #25)

The core advertises `1.0.0.0/24` and `2606:4700:4700::/48` with AS path `64999 13335`, community `65000:777` and large community `65000:777:1`. No other route carries AS 64999 or these communities, so each capture below is complete and holds only these routes. `lab/scripts/verify-policy-matrix.py` uses the same routes. All captures are from 28 October 2026.

- `frr-live/aspath4.json`, `aspath6.json`, `community4.json`, `community6.json`: FRRouting 10.2.2, `vtysh -c 'show bgp <ipv4|ipv6> unicast regexp _64999_ json'` and `... community 65000:777 json`.
- `vyos-live/aspath6.json`, `community6.json`: VyOS 1.5 stream (FRRouting 9.1.3), the same commands for IPv6.
- `arista-live/aspath6.json`: cEOS 4.36.3M, `show ipv6 bgp regexp _64999_ | json`. EOS regexp output carries no communities.
- `arista-live/community4_detail.json`, `community6_detail.json`: cEOS 4.36.3M, `show bgp <ipv4|ipv6> unicast community 65000:777 detail | json`. This form carries `communityList` and `largeCommunityList`, and the IPv6 form matches IPv6 routes, unlike `show ipv6 bgp community`. Issue #66.
- `mikrotik-live/aspath.json`, `community.json`: RouterOS 7.16.2 raw responses for `_64999_` and `65000:777`, extracted from the lab JSONL query log with their original timestamp, device and query.
- `frr-live/community4_detail.json`, `community6_detail.json`: FRRouting 10.2.2, `vtysh -c 'show bgp <ipv4|ipv6> unicast community 65000:777 json detail'`. Routes are keyed by prefix with a `paths` list of detail paths, which carry communities. `regexp` has no `json detail` form. Issue #67.
- `vyos-live/community4_detail.json`, `community6_detail.json`: VyOS 1.5 stream (FRRouting 9.1.3), `vtysh -c 'show bgp <ipv4|ipv6> unicast community 65000:777 json detail'`. Issue #71.
- `juniper-live/`: vJunos-router 26.2R1.7, 29 October 2026. `aspath<4|6>.xml` and `community<4|6>.xml` use `show route protocol bgp table <inet.0|inet6.0> aspath-regex ".* 64999 .*" detail | display xml` and `... community 65000:777 detail | display xml`. `route4.xml` and `route6.xml` use `show route protocol bgp table <inet.0|inet6.0> <1.0.0.0/24|2606:4700:4700::/48> best detail | display xml` and keep every ADD-PATH path the core sends. Junos prints large communities as `large:65000:777:1`; the parser removes the prefix. `trace.txt` uses `traceroute inet 1.1.1.1 wait 1 source 10.250.6.1`. Issue #82.
- `juniper-live/community4-otc.xml`: vJunos-router 26.2R1.7, 30 October 2026, `show route protocol bgp table inet.0 community 37195:302 detail | display xml`, trimmed to 1.0.0.0/24 and 8.44.61.0/24 with one path each. The 8.44.61.0/24 path carries the Only-to-Customer attribute (RFC 9234), so Junos emits two `<bgp-path-attributes>` blocks. Issue #133.
- `cisco-ios-live/`: Cisco IOL 17.18.02 (IOS XE), 29 October 2026. `route<4|6>.txt` use `show bgp <ipv4|ipv6> unicast <prefix> | exclude pathid:|Epoch`, `aspath<4|6>.txt` use `show bgp <ipv4|ipv6> unicast quote-regexp "_64999_"`, `community<4|6>.txt` use `show bgp <ipv4|ipv6> unicast community 65000:777`, and `trace.txt` uses `traceroute 1.1.1.1 timeout 1 probe 2 source 10.250.9.1`. `route_aggregated4.txt` (`show bgp ipv4 unicast 1.1.1.1 | exclude pathid:|Epoch`) carries an aggregator note after the AS path. `community_bulk4.txt` (`show bgp ipv4 unicast community 13335:10020`) is complete, with 35 routes from the lab table. Trailing whitespace is removed. The core sends IOL its best path only. Issue #83.

## On-demand Cisco platforms (issues #99 and #100)

The lab probe advertises `1.1.1.0/24` and `2606:4700::/44` with AS path `65000 13335` and community `37195:302`. Each appliance has one eBGP session to the probe, so every capture is complete and holds only these routes. Captures are from the text Ultraglass instance on 29 October 2026, with trailing whitespace removed. `test_live_captures_cisco.py` runs them through their parsers.

- `cisco-xr-live/`: XRd 24.2.11 (IOS-XR). `route<4|6>.txt` use `show bgp <ipv4|ipv6> unicast <target>`, `aspath<4|6>.txt` and `community<4|6>.txt` the built-in regexp and community filters, `ping<4|6>.txt` the built-in ping, and `trace<4|6>.txt` use `traceroute <ipv4|ipv6> <target> timeout 1 probe 2 source <source>`. IOS-XR has no structured BGP parser yet (#113).
- `cisco-nxos-live/`: Nexus 9300v Lite, NX-OS 10.4(8). The same file set from the built-in NX-OS directives. NX-OS has no structured BGP parser yet (#110).
- `cisco-iosv-live/`: IOSv 15.9(3)M6. The same file set. `trace6.txt` comes from the lab's custom traceroute directive, because IOSv 15.9 IPv6 traceroute accepts only a destination. The IOS parser reads the BGP captures. Summary output (`aspath`, `community`) carries no communities, and the tests check that none are invented.

## Huawei VRPv8 (issue #103)

- `huawei-vrpv8-live/`: CE12800 V200R005C10SPC607B607, which runs VRP 8.180 (VRPv8). The rc.2 run queried it as `lab-huawei` with platform `huawei`; the lab now names it `lab-huawei-vrpv8` with platform `huawei_vrpv8`. Both platforms share directives and parsers and differ only in the netmiko class. The files are raw responses from the text instance's rc.2 lab run on 30 October 2026 (archive query log), with trailing whitespace removed. `aspath4.txt` and `aspath6.txt` use `display bgp [ipv6] routing-table regular-expression _13335$`, `community4.txt` and `community6.txt` use `display bgp [ipv6] routing-table community 37195:302`, `route4.txt` uses `display bgp routing-table 1.1.1.1 | no-more`, `ping4.txt` uses `ping -c 5 -a 10.250.8.1 1.1.1.1`, and `trace4.txt` uses `tracert -w 500 -q 1 -f 1 -a 10.250.8.1 1.1.1.1`. The lab feeds this node a capped route subset, so the IPv6 community table is empty. `route4.txt` prints the AS path in asdot (`5.280`).
- `huawei-vrpv8-live/route4_vpn_instance.txt`: anonymised user capture from a VRPv8 NE router, `display bgp vpnv4 vpn-instance inet routing-table 8.8.8.0 24`. Two paths for one prefix; the second carries the route-target ext-community `RT <64501 : 1>`. Addresses are documentation ranges and the operator ASNs are private; the origin AS and prefix are real.
- `test_live_captures_huawei_vrpv8.py` runs every capture through its parser. The traceroute capture parses to a hop table through the Huawei traceroute parser. Ping has no structured parser, so the test checks the capture is complete.

## 1 November 2026 onboarding captures

- `cumulus-vx54-live/{default,lab}-community{4,6}.json`: complete unedited Cumulus VX 5.4.0 responses, FRRouting `7.5+cl5.3.0u0`, from the separate acceptance agent's isolated QEMU VM. Copied byte-for-byte from `/tmp/opencode/cumulus77-vx54/captures/`; `manifest.json` there records each command. Commands are `sudo -n vtysh -c 'show bgp [vrf LAB] <ipv4|ipv6> unicast community 65000:777 json detail'`. Default VRF carries `1.0.0.0/24` and `2606:4700:4700::/48`; LAB carries `198.51.100.0/24` and `2001:db8:100::/48`. Each per-prefix list starts with prefix/advertisedTo metadata, followed by one BGP path (#217). Parser tests replay these captures; they do not prove a fresh appliance run of the fix.
- `cisco-iosv-live/aspath_policy4.txt` and `aspath_policy6.txt`: IOSv 15.9(3)M6, complete `show bgp <ipv4|ipv6> unicast quote-regexp "_13335$"` responses from the failed structured onboarding query in #128. Extracted from `ultraglass-lab-evidence/2026-11-01-onboard-128/ultraglass/lab-iosv/onboard.json`; only trailing whitespace is removed. Each response holds two routes, including the active policy fixture. The long IPv6 prefix wraps, and its continuation starts one column right of the header (#215).
